Subject: MSA / Order Form - security exhibit questions and pen test access

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our security team reviewed the security exhibit and has a few asks before we can move to legal redlines:

- We need explicit audit rights language that allows a yearly inspection or an alternative equivalent (SOC 2 + pen test evidence).
- Clarify pen test notice windows and whether they can run an external vendor (we typically require 30–45 days notice).
- Request a SOC 2 crosswalk mapping the relevant assertions to production controls and a cadence for evidence (we prefer quarterly evidence summaries for the first year).

I've attached the document our legal team will use to capture redlines; happy to take a short call to walk through.

Best,
Alice Thompson
VP, IT Risk & Compliance
MediCore Health

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form - security exhibit questions and pen test access

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on staying collaborative here. Quick notes and proposed next steps: 

1) Mutual action plan: we'll propose two pathways to satisfy audit needs:
   - Primary: provide annual SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where needed) + a summarized penetration test report (high level findings) plus a quarterly evidence summary for the first 12 months (control attestations, patch cadence, incident ops summary).
   - Alternative: limited inspection (one per year) with strict scope/timebox and an approved vendor; Redwood to require 30 days notice and supervise access to production (read-only consoles, ephemeral creds, scoped logs).

2) Pen test windows: Redwood's baseline is one vendor-verified external assessment per 12 months. For any customer-requested pen tests we ask for 30–45 days notice and that testing is limited in blast radius and timed windows.

3) Evidence cadence: we can commit to quarterly exec-level summaries for the first year, then move to semi-annual thereafter. Full artifact exchange (raw logs, config dumps) will be via controlled evidence exchanges and only as scoped by the exhibit (not full access).

I'm looping in legal and security for specific redline language. Laura / Karthik — can you propose guarded wording for the Order Form exhibit and an inspection-lite clause we can share back with MediCore? I'll schedule a 30-minute sync if helpful.

—Sergio
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Quick draft language and guardrails (high level) we should push: 

- "Audit rights": Customer may request an audit no more than once in any 12-month period. The parties will first rely on Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report (covering relevant Trust Services Criteria). If the SOC 2 does not provide sufficient assurance for Customer's specified control objective, Customer may request a focused inspection limited to identified control areas. Inspection subject to: 30 days prior written notice; mutually agreed scope; remote-only unless expressly agreed; non-production testing prohibited.

- "Penetration testing": Customer-authorized pen tests allowed once per year via a pre-approved vendor list. Tests must be limited to non-destructive techniques, scheduled in a mutually-agreed window, with a 30–45 day notice period. All findings to be shared as a redacted executive summary; raw exploit/POC materials retained by Redwood for incident analysis only.

- "Evidence cadence": For first 12 months after go-live Redwood to provide quarterly control summaries and access to SOC 2 report and pen test executive summaries. Ongoing: semi-annual summaries. For requests outside the cadence, parties to follow an evidence request playbook (attach as exhibit).

Attachments I'm adding: SOC2_summary_2027.pdf (internal summary we can share), PenTest_Scope_Sample.xlsx (example scope we can offer to customers).

If Legal is good with the high level I'll convert to MSA redline markup and share.

Karthik
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Couple of legal clarifications / proposed contract text snippets: 

- Limit inspection rights to: (a) receipt of SOC 2 Type II report and (b) one focused inspection per 12 months limited to agreed control families. Insert a confidentiality & redaction paragraph that prevents disclosure of infrastructure designs or other customers' data.

- Add an approval flow: Customer submits proposed scope + vendor details; Redwood reserves right to reject vendor for cause and to require reasonable constraints. Add a requirement for a mutually executed NDA for vendor access.

- For pen tests: we will accept executive summaries only for sharing externally; raw technical artifacts may be shared under additional agreements for due-diligence but not as part of the standard exhibit.

I will prepare an MSA redline with bracketed alternatives (inspection-lite vs SOC2-only) and send that back by EOD tomorrow. Also recommend adding an evidence playbook link into the Order Form so procurement has a single place to follow the cadence.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
